blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — El Niño does not mean no rain. Engr. Al Quiblat, chief of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) Visayas, urged Cebu residents not to read the rain still falling as proof that El Niño has spared the province, even as forecasts point to below-normal rainfall by November and drought by March. That misconception can delay preparation for a phenomenon that has already reached strong levels in the Tropical Pacific and could climb to “very strong” by the end of 2026, Pagasa said.
